items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: I didn't know nothing about him, you know, but Henry told me after I found out

ctx.x: Well did you make him happy when you hit him?

He just laid there. The Henry Bowser was a bartender. Yeah. Henry Bowser, cause I was fixing to hit him another league, so I just jumped over the counter and grab him. I said, man, you know who you hit? I said, I don't give a damn who I hit with or I don't care about it. He said, you hit one of the best guys around you. Boy, that man is crazy about you, you could get anything you want from him. I said, I ain't studying nothing. Was he rich? He was rich? Oh, but he was, he was, he was a big shot around there, big…
Oh, he was a madam. He was a madam of the house.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: I know the bartender called Henry Bowser... He was bartending at that time around there.

ctx.x: Do you think one of the Lalas ran 25s at one time?

I don't remember. No. I used to bum around there all the time, but I never knew who owned the place and who run it. I know the bartender called Henry Bowser, which used to be bartending around there in that time, you know, big brown-skinned fella. Henry Bowser? J-Henry Bowser. Bowser. Bowser, yeah. He was bartending at that time around there. When me and Mineta was playing at Parkish Place there, 101.
Did they have a place to dance in 25s? No.
